entry_state: This is a separate affected-chapter regression, beginning at chapter 9. The reader needs to distinguish economic events, reporting treatments and company labels before following the finite company forecast; the preceding eight chapters have not been reread in this stream.

findings.judgment: 9.1 separates economic terms, reporting treatments and company labels. Rule-package dates and adoption conditions prevent the 2026 setting from automatically selecting IFRS 18; IFRS, US GAAP and ASBE evidence limits remain visible.

9.2 introduces ordinary operating states before 9.3 uses identical purchases (10 at 5 and 10 at 7) and a delivery of 12. FIFO gives cost 64 and stock 56, LIFO 80/40 and weighted average 72/48. Company policy does not become universal ASC authority.

A write-down of 6 and reversal of 4 retain the original-cost ceiling. 9.4 distinguishes performance, billing, collection, receipt, consumption, payment, depreciation and payroll; no hidden loan or balancing plug supplies missing cash.

The simple-contract recurrence states its no-advance and no-impairment restrictions. R=60, B=50, C=30 gives AR=20 and CA=10; B=80 instead gives AR=50 and CL=20. Cumulative service costs 40 then 70 post increments 40 then 30. The advance example explains why gross billing and the remaining unconditional right differ.

G, A, K and C are staged before T=G+A−K and the advance recurrence. The net-assets control reduces exactly to earned R because applied credit K is counted once. Conditions on K and collections prevent duplicate allocation and overcollection. A wholly prepaid invoice changes contract state even with no monetary posting.

The state-only proposal has empty lines but an independently checked economic delta. Authorization, exact replay, identity conflict, stale opening and exhausted credit remain distinct. Export must retain the consumed allocation or report unsupported lossless export; balanced or unchanged accounts cannot establish a valid event. The final paragraph introduces return obligations without implying that service costs or tax are already known.

four_ledgers.reader_comprehension: The inventory comparison establishes why book labels are insufficient; the customer-contract example then separates earned consideration, unconditional rights, cash and used advance credits. The state-only example explains a consequence that monetary balances alone cannot expose.
four_ledgers.mathematical_integrity: Inventory arithmetic and the simple/advance recurrences were checked locally under their stated single-contract assumptions. This is exposition and finite-arithmetic evidence, not a new accounting method or executable-runtime check.
four_ledgers.source_fidelity: Selected AASB 15 periods, paragraph anchors and limitations remain explicit. No current jurisdictional admission, US/ASBE implementation or real-company authorization is inferred.
four_ledgers.typography: 113–118 were read at normal resolution. Equations, the state-only record and their surrounding qualifications are visible; no new confirmed layout defect.

exit_state: Customer advances now preserve both monetary balances and consumed-credit history. Performance, billing, collection and replay remain separate. The next example must explain how delivered goods can create a refund obligation and a separately measured right to recover inventory; missing service costs and tax remain inputs to the full statements.
